bullets.title: MU: Citi raises PT to $1,200 on DRAM ASP +200% and supply undersupply through 2027
bullets.body: Citi raised MU FY26/27 EPS estimates by 4-10% and lifted PT to $1,200 (10x CY27E EPS) as DRAM spot prices are up 52% since January and 21% above contract pricing, implying contracts should move higher. Global DRAM expected 5% undersupplied in 2026 with ASPs forecast +200% for the year; NAND ASPs +186%. MU F27E EPS of $114.73 is 4% above Street; Dell reportedly already signed long-term agreements.

bullets.title: AVGO: JPM's Harlan Sur bullish, recommends doubling down on weakness; XPU targeting $250-300B FY28 revenue
bullets.body: JPMorgan's Harlan Sur hosting an AMA on AVGO, bullish despite recent weakness and looking through Asia supply chain noise. Separately, AVGO's XPV first tranche funds Anthropic FY26 purchases; full funding would allow volumes to triple to 15GW in FY28, with AVGO targeting $250-300B FY28 XPU revenue at $10-15B content per GW.

bullets.title: INTC: 18A-P in risk production — potential Apple foundry deal catalyst
bullets.body: Intel began risk production of its advanced 18A-P chip node at the VLSI Symposium, meeting initial timeline expectations. Multiple desks flagged this as a potential catalyst toward an Apple foundry deal; Mizuho notes INTC supply constrained through 2027E as agentic AI server demand rises, with Coral Rapids targeting 2028 server CPU leadership.

bullets.title: HPE: Citi reiterates Buy; JPM OW; management reaffirms double-digit FY27 growth on AI networking
bullets.body: HPE Discover event consensus bullish: Citi reiterates Buy and JPM maintains OW citing FY27 pipeline multiples of current backlog, supply constraints keeping backlog elevated through FY26, and Juniper/Aruba integration strengthening full-stack AI infrastructure positioning. FY26 networking revenue guidance approaching +10%; FY27 guide +8-12%. AMD Helios design-win announced with QFX5252 switch.

bullets.title: SNAP: SPECS AR glasses launched at $2,195 — Citi Neutral, KeyBanc Sector Weight; execution risk dominates near-term
bullets.body: Snap unveiled SPECS AR glasses at AWE 2026 launching Fall 2026 at $2,195 with 51° FOV (vs. Meta Ray-Ban's 20°), 4-hour battery, and standalone operation. V1 stretch goal is ~100K units targeting the 450K+ developer community. Both Citi and KeyBanc flag multiple generations needed for mass adoption; price must decline materially for broader uptake.

bullets.title: SNOW/PLTR: Databricks investor day read-across bullish — limited competitive overlap, Databricks at $6.9B ARR
bullets.body: UBS and Jefferies both note Databricks ($6.9B ARR, 80% growth) sees strong complementarity with Palantir and minimal share loss risk for Snowflake (SQL data warehouse at $1.5B run-rate, 100% growth). Enterprise AI token cost pushback is a near-term speed bump but not a secular slowdown. UBS remains Buy-rated on both SNOW and PLTR.

bullets.title: AMD: 30MW AI compute deal with Rackspace; negative 3P DC checks for Q2 flagged
bullets.body: AMD signed a 30MW AI compute deal with Rackspace starting late 2026-28 per UBS. However, JPM flagged negative third-party checks showing AMD data center revenues slowing on CPU deployments in Q2, cited as one driver of recent tech sector weakness.

bullets.title: FSLR: Bernstein initiates Underperform with $217 PT — 18% downside
bullets.body: Bernstein initiated First Solar at Underperform with a $217 price target, implying approximately 18% downside. The initiation is part of an 11-name clean energy sector launch; FSLR is the only Underperform, with CEG, GEV, and VST receiving Outperform ratings.

bullets.title: FIG: Citi initiates Buy at $36 PT — Q2 estimates 7-9pts above consensus, AI seat upgrades key driver
bullets.body: Citi initiated Figma at Buy/High Risk with a $36 PT (9.4x FY27E EV/revenue). Proprietary checks show strong Full Seat upgrades and AI credit utilization; Q2/FY26E revenue estimates 7-9 points above consensus. FIG sits at only 4% TAM penetration with TAM potentially doubling to $50B by 2029.

bullets.title: MSFT: Shifting Copilot to multi-model architecture; exploring DeepSeek for low-cost inference
bullets.body: Multiple desks note Microsoft is transitioning Copilot away from OpenAI exclusivity toward multi-model orchestration using Anthropic (Claude) and evaluating DeepSeek for low-cost inference. Economics are the driver — usage-based pricing requires controlling inference cost. Separately, a $3B cloud infrastructure deal with ORCL reportedly fell through.

bullets.title: AMZN: FTC drafting complaint over advertiser deception — billions in civil penalties at risk
bullets.body: The FTC has drafted a potential complaint against Amazon over claims it misled advertisers, with multiple state AGs also involved. A lawsuit or settlement could come as soon as summer 2026, with potential civil penalties in the billions of dollars.

bullets.title: MU earnings preview: consensus $20.25 EPS, $35.06B revenue — call Wed June 24
bullets.body: MU reports Wednesday June 24 at 4:30PM ET; FactSet consensus $20.25 EPS and $35.06B revenue. UBS prefers MU as a top US semi pick on DRAM/NAND pricing upcycle. Citi's $1,200 PT represents 4% above Street on FY27E EPS of $114.73.

bullets.title: AAOI: +3.4% pre-market on credit line; management roadshow bullish on ramp to $1.4B quarterly run-rate
bullets.body: AAOI's subsidiary entered a one-year credit agreement with Shanghai Pudong Development Bank, lifting shares 3.4% pre-market. Wolfe Research (Peer Perform) notes management guides transceiver revenue to ramp from $81M in Q1'26 to $1.4B quarterly run-rate by mid-2027 with design wins at Microsoft, Oracle, and Amazon, but cites execution risk and expensive valuation as reasons to wait.

bullets.title: T: CFO Pascal Desroches retiring Dec 31; Jennifer Biry appointed successor — KeyBanc OW, $36 PT
bullets.body: AT&T CFO Pascal Desroches will retire December 31, 2026; Jennifer Biry (ex-McAfee CFO/COO, former AT&T executive) appointed Deputy CFO effective July 6 and will assume CFO role January 1, 2027. KeyBanc maintains Overweight with $36 PT, calling the transition well-planned. T traded down ~0.9% after-hours on the news.

bullets.title: RBLX: Short squeeze driven by Grow a Garden 2 CCU data strength
bullets.body: Jefferies notes RBLX is seeing a squeeze driven by strong Grow a Garden 2 concurrent user data with platform CCU up week-over-week, creating potential short squeeze into the weekend. Risk of reset flagged if data prints weaker on Monday.

bullets.title: MRVL: Hedgeye flags as long on SPX rebalancing flows
bullets.body: Hedgeye is long MRVL citing SPX rebalancing catalyst and views it as an inclusion-driven trade, distinct from broader Mag-7 and AI infrastructure crowding concerns. Separately, Semis & Semi Equipment allocations more than doubled YTD at hedge funds to record highs per Goldman Prime.

bullets.title: DKNG: MS notes deposits tracking ahead of Q2 consensus; ~70-75% combined share with FanDuel
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley data using Carbon Arc credit/debit card panel shows Big 3 operators (FanDuel/DraftKings/BetMGM) with ~5% Q2 customer deposit growth; DKNG and FanDuel maintaining ~70-75% combined deposit share and both running ahead of Q2 revenue consensus estimates. Kalshi and Fanatics gaining sequential share.

bullets.title: ACN: Two bolt-on acquisitions announced ahead of June 18 earnings (est. $3.71 EPS, $18.78B rev)
bullets.body: Accenture announced two acquisitions: Industries eXcellence Group (IndX), a Siemens software division for manufacturers with 650+ professionals, and Alfahealth (subsidiary of Engineering Group) adding ~1,200 health professionals to ACN's Italy practice. Both deals are undisclosed in size. ACN reports Thursday June 18 at 8AM ET.

bullets.title: GOOGL: UK CMA imposes new conduct requirements on search ranking and data portability
bullets.body: The UK CMA introduced two new conduct requirements for Google's general search services under the digital markets regime: improved transparency/fairness in search result ranking and the ability for users to port search data to authorized third-party firms. CMA signaled willingness to bring additional measures if needed.

bullets.title: Semi capex equipment: Citi raises AMAT to $710, LRCX to $450, KLAC to $290 on WFE bull case to $250B by 2028
bullets.body: Citi updated its WFE bull case to $145B/$200B/$250B in CY26/27/28, lifting AMAT PT to $710 (31x CY28 P/E, +30%/+22% Y/Y rev growth), LRCX to $450 (40x CY28), and KLAC to $290 (40x CY28). DRAM supply constraints are driving structural NAND demand increases for agentic AI, requiring 2-4 new greenfield fabs or $15-30B in NAND WFE.
